title: Criteria Expression
description: One deliberately dumb expression type serving four features: kill criteria, success criteria, scoring vetoes, and platform assertions. It is not a language and must not become one — no arithmetic, no functions, no string interpolation. If a rule cannot be said here, write prose in the stage procedure and require a human to judge it.

operator.description:
Ordering operators (gt, gte, lt, lte) require both sides to be numbers; a non-number on either side is an evaluation error, never a silent false.

`in` and `not_in` are containment, and which way round depends on the measured value:
  - measured value is an ARRAY — `in` holds when every element of `right` is present in it. This is the 'required element is present' reading, and it is the one platform profiles use: `{left: package.locales, op: in, right: [ru]}` asks whether the package ships Russian, not whether the whole locale list equals [ru].
  - measured value is a SCALAR — `in` holds when it appears in `right`.
The distinction matters because reading it the other way makes every locale assertion pass vacuously, and those assertions are blocking on three platforms.

`exists` and `absent` test only for the presence of the measured value and omit `right`. A value of null counts as absent.

left.description: A dimension id from core/reference/dimensions.yaml, a metric name, or a dotted artifact path such as 'game_design.session.target_seconds'.

right.description: Literal only. Omitted for exists/absent, and mutually exclusive with right_path.

right_path.description:
A dotted path, resolved the same way as `left`, for comparing two measured values against each other — a session against the platform's interstitial interval, an asset estimate against the budget it has to fit.

It is a separate key rather than a convention on `right` because `right: casual` and `right: platform.capabilities.ads` are both bare strings, and nothing mechanical can tell a literal from a path. One of the two has to be declared, and declaring the rarer one keeps every existing literal unchanged.

then.description: A comparison has one right-hand side. Giving both is a rule whose meaning depends on which the evaluator happens to read first.

namedCriterion.description: An expression with an identity and a reason, so an evaluation result is explainable rather than just true/false.

rationale.description: Why this threshold. A criterion nobody can justify will be argued away at the gate.

criterionResult.description: The recorded outcome of evaluating a namedCriterion, stored so a gate decision can be re-read later.
